title: operator-session-jwt-escrow-and-audit-nonce-anchoring
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce risk of operator-session replay and accidental cross-tenant key usage by introducing an ephemeral operator JWT escrow flow tied to KMS-wrapped operator session keys, and anchor audit events with a nonce signed using the same escrow key. This PR implements session-scoped RBAC tokens for operators, a KMS escrow/unescrow handshake to wrap ephemeral session keys with customer CMKs (when available), and an audit nonce anchoring mechanism so every mutating operator action can be tied cryptographically to the operator session.

What changed (high level):
- Add session-scoped RBAC support: operator sessions can be created with ephemeral claims that expire and are revocable via the new session manager. Sessions are represented by a short-lived JWT plus a session-id that must be presented for operator API calls.
- KMS escrow: when a tenant provides a CMK, the session manager will request an escrow-wrapped session key (EncryptUsingKey) and store only the wrapped blob. Service-side operations that need to act on behalf of the tenant will unescrow (Decrypt) via a tight audit path that logs the key-id used. For hosted tenants without CMKs, the platform fallback uses a platform-wrapped ephemeral key with additional operator-scoped constraints.
- Audit nonce anchoring: every operator mutation now requires a per-session monotonic nonce signed with the session key. The audit writer records nonce, session-id, operator-id, and wrapped-key-id; a validation layer rejects out-of-order or replayed nonces for the session.
- Observation and metrics: added session lifecycle metrics (sessions_created, sessions_revoked, unescrow_calls_total), audit_nonce_rejections, and a per-tenant KMS-wrap proportion gauge.
- Docs and migration: docs/rbac/session-scoped-roles.md and upgrade notes describing optional tenant CMK onboarding, rollback plan, and canary rollout strategy.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Backwards compatible: existing operator tokens remain valid; new sessions opt-in via the feature flag "session_escrow_enabled" at operator-account level.
- Canary: rollout plan included: start in staging, enable for internal tenant 42, monitor audit_nonce_rejections and unescrow latencies, then enable for 10% of production operator traffic before full rollout.
- Fallbacks: if KMS unescrow fails, request is rejected by default for tenants with CMKs; for non-CMK tenants we fall back to platform-wrapped key path and emit a security audit event.

Security considerations:
- Limits and quotas: throttled KMS unescrow calls to avoid accidental key-exhaustion; per-operator session rate limits enforced.
- Key exposure: the service never stores unwrapped session keys; unwrapped keys live only in an in-memory enclave for the duration of the operation and are zeroized afterwards.
- Audit retention: audit records include wrapped-key-id but not raw key material. Migration to longer retention for tenant keys is opt-in and controlled by retention_policy features.

Migration checklist (in-PR):
- [x] feature flag and operator API gate
- [x] session manager with revoke endpoint and server-side tests
- [x] KMS escrow glue and integration tests (mocked KMS + small e2e)
- [x] audit writer changes and nonce validator
- [x] docs and upgrade guide + Linear ticket references
- [x] metrics + dashboard draft

Related: Linear ENG-1987 (operator-session-escrow design), ENG-2041 (audit-pipeline-consistency). SUP-4219 captures a customer request to bind operator actions to tenant CMKs for audits.

release_notes: Operator session escrow + audit nonce anchoring: Introduces ephemeral session-scoped operator tokens with optional tenant CMK escrow, KMS-wrapped session keys, and nonce-based replay protection for operator mutations. Feature is behind the 'session_escrow_enabled' feature flag and is opt-in per-tenant. See docs/rbac/session-scoped-roles.md for migration steps.
notes_for_ops: Rollout steps: enable flag in staging -> enable for internal tenant 42 -> monitor metrics (audit_nonce_rejections, unescrow_latency_ms, sessions_revoked) -> 10% production canary -> full rollout. Emergency rollback: disable feature flag which returns system to legacy operator token behaviour. If KMS unescrow errors spike, set tenant to fallback-mode via admin console.
security_review_summary: Threat model updated: operator replay attacks mitigated by signed nonces + monotonic session counters. KMS usage is audited with wrapped_key_id and rate-limited. New in-memory enclave ensures unwrapped keys do not persist. No plaintext keys written to storage. Recommended follow-ups: HSM attestation for enclave and short-lived CMK aliases for high-risk tenants.
motivation_summary: Customer and internal audits requested stronger cryptographic binding between operator actions and tenant keys. This PR provides a practical, opt-in path that ties operator sessions to tenant CMKs and improves audit traceability while minimizing platform key exposure.
